title: Micro-impact architect — weekly OKR sketch & retro
body:
Context:
- Trying a different mental model this quarter: think like an ‘impact architect’ — small scaffolding changes that multiplicatively increase throughput of my teammates and infra. Focus on compound wins not heroic single features.

Quarter Objective (personal): Increase downstream developer velocity for model rollouts by 20% (measured via time-to-first-successful-deploy for model variants I touch).
Key Results (draft):
- KR1: Reduce average time-to-first-successful-deploy from 6.2h -> 5.0h for my owned routes (baseline measured Dec).
- KR2: Ship 3 lightweight infra templates (deploy + smoke test) for common model variants by end of Q1.
- KR3: Create 2 checklist-driven runbooks and get 2 teams to adopt them.

This week (snapshot): 2025-02-24 — 2025-03-02
- Commitments I made: finish template v1, unblock SRE on canary rollback probe, pair on smoke test harness with Rafi.
- Reality: template v1 at 70% (missing docs + env matrix), rollback probe blocking due to flaky probe in k8s sidecar, paired session went well but follow-up required.
- Time log (rough): dev 14h, meetings 6h, pairing 3h, docs 2h. Too many context switches on Wed -> lower focus blocks.

Quick wins discovered:
- Small fixture in smoke tests (reduce teardown delay) shaved ~8 minutes per run for local dev loop. Multiply by 10 devs = 80 minutes saved/day (estimate).
- A small README tweak helped Sarah onboard the template earlier than expected. Docs are leverage.

Hypotheses to test next week:
- H1: If I add an explicit 'minimal env matrix' set to template, first-time deploys drop by 15%. Test with 5 teams on canary.
- H2: If rollback probe includes a second coarse-grain healthcheck (service-level), false positives drop and SRE signal noise improves.

Risks / Blockers:
- CI minutes budget could constrain heavy smoke-test runs — need to coordinate with infra budget owners (file RL-2345 ticket).
- Context switching near EOD reduces deep work; try batching meeting blocks to Tue/Thu mornings.

Experiment backlog (prioritized):
1) Finish template v1 + minimal env matrix (high impact, medium effort).
2) Add a 'dev-loop' quickstart script to reduce local iteration time (low effort).
3) Automate smoke test teardown to avoid flakiness (medium effort, depends on CI infra).

Retrospective notes (what worked / what didn't):
- Worked: pairing with Rafi produced concrete test improvements; quick README tweak had outsized impact.
- Didn't: tried to land too many edits in one PR; reviewers overwhelmed -> slower merges. Lesson: smaller PRs.

Concrete next week plan (top 3):
- Monday: finish minimal env matrix + update README. Ship PR for template v1 by EOD.
- Tuesday: meet with infra budget owner (15m) to confirm CI minutes for smoke-test schedule.
- Wednesday: implement dev-loop quickstart, test locally, demo Thu AM.

Signals to watch (metrics):
- time-to-first-successful-deploy (per-route) — main northstar.
- local smoke-test turnaround time.
- PR size (lines changed) and review latency.
- number of manual rollbacks triggered during canary.

Notes to self / TODO snippets:
- TODO: add a tiny checklist at top of template PR describing how to smoke-test locally (copy from smoke-harness repo).
- Keep PRs < 300 LOC if possible.
- If review stalls >48h, ping reviewer + add context summary.

Loose thoughts / brain dump:
- Could we add a "first-run" telemetry ping for template runs (opt-in) so we can measure adoption without manual check-ins? Privacy filter obviously.
- Maybe run a short office-hours slot for teams to try template with me (30m weekly). Could accelerate adoption.

End-of-week self-grade: B- 
- Reasons: shipped partial, found high-leverage tweaks, but context switching slowed completion.

Open questions for manager check-in:
- How to prioritize cross-team onboarding vs shipping more templates?
- Any slack in squad capacity for handling CI minute increases?

Catch-all: keep this doc lean. Move finalized procedures to confluence + link from template README.
